titel: Hotel near Venray town centre | Hotel Asteria
omschrijving: Stay a 6-minute drive from Venray town centre. Shopping on the Grotestraat, a terrace on the Grote Markt and then wellness and dinner at Hotel Asteria.
hero-sub: Shopping streets, three squares with terraces and the Great Church, a six-minute drive from your hotel room.
hero-alt: The Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk with its tall tower in the centre of Venray
oog-kop: Venray town centre at a glance
t2-waarde: Mon 12 noon-6 pm, Tue-Thu 9.30 am-6 pm, Sat until 5 pm
t5-waarde: Blue zone 2 hours free, car park €1.50 per hour (2026)
v1-p1: From Hotel Asteria it is a 6-minute drive to the centre of Venray, or 20 minutes by bike. The centre is compact: the Grotestraat is the main shopping street and links the Grote Markt with the Henseniusplein. Together with the Schouwburgplein, these are the three squares where the terraces are.
v1-p2: The shops open from 12 noon on Mondays and from 9.30 am Tuesday to Saturday. Friday is late shopping until 9 pm, although each shop decides for itself whether it opens. On Mondays the weekly market is held on the Henseniusplein and the Schouwburgplein from 11 am to 4 pm.
v1-alt: Shoppers on the Grotestraat in Venray, with stepped gables and the roof of the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk
v1-knop: Shopping and going out on venray.nl
v2-kop: The Great Church and the museum
v2-p1: On the Grote Markt stands the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk, known in Venray simply as the Great Church (Grote Kerk). It is a late Gothic church from the fifteenth century and a national monument. The tower was lost in the war winter of 1944 and was later rebuilt. Inside is a remarkable collection of statues, including eleven sixteenth-century apostle figures against the pillars.
v2-p2: Opposite the church is the Venrays Museum, about the history of the region. It is open from Wednesday to Sunday, 1.30 pm to 5 pm. A ticket costs €5 and the Dutch Museumkaart is valid.
v2-alt: Terraces under the trees on the Grote Markt in Venray
v3-p1: A twenty-minute walk from the Grote Markt is the Odapark, a wooded park with a sculpture forest. The sculpture forest is open every day from sunrise to sunset and admission is free. The pavilion has changing exhibitions and you can get a drink there. Dogs are welcome on a lead and there is a charging point for e-bikes.
v3-alt: Large grey sculpture of two stylised figures among the trees in the Odapark, Venray
tip: Take the bike into town. You are there in twenty minutes and can leave it for free in the guarded, covered bike park on the Leeuwstraat, next to the library. You can charge your e-bike there too. You can hire bikes from us at reception.
g1-tekst: Monday from 12 noon, Tuesday to Saturday from 9.30 am. Late shopping on Friday until 9 pm.

g2-tekst: Every Monday from 11 am to 4 pm on the Henseniusplein and the Schouwburgplein.
g2-alt: Empty terrace chairs and closed parasols under the trees by the Grote Markt in Venray
g3-tekst: In the blue zone you can park for 2 hours free with a parking disc. The Centrumgarage costs €1.50 per hour, up to €5 a day.

g4-tekst: The sculpture forest is open every day from sunrise to sunset. Admission is free.

dag-kop: How to make a day of it
dag-sub: A relaxed breakfast, a day in town and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 am to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 am to 10.30 am at weekends. The shops open at 9.30 am, so there is no rush.
m2-tekst: Shop along the Grotestraat, have lunch on one of the three squares and then drop in at the Venrays Museum or walk on to the Odapark.
m2-alt: Side wall and tower of the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk in Venray against a blue sky
m3-tekst: Six minutes later you are back at the hotel and in the sauna. The wellness area is open from 4 pm to 10 pm Monday to Thursday and from 12 noon to 10 pm Friday to Sunday. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m4-tekst: No need to go out again: in the hotel brasserie you can have dinner until 9.30 pm.
kamers-sub: That way you combine a day in town with an evening in the sauna. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: The town centre lies south-west of the hotel. The map also shows three days out for another day.
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria, the centre of Venray and three other days out
f1-v: How far is Venray town centre from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 3.6 kilometres to the Grote Markt, about 6 minutes by car. By bike it is 3 kilometres, around 20 minutes. You can also walk: that is 2.9 kilometres, about 40 minutes.
f2-v: Where can I park in the centre of Venray?
f2-a: A blue zone applies in and around the centre: with a parking disc you can park there for 2 hours free. For longer stays there is the Centrumgarage on the Langeweg and the Blekersveld and Raadhuisstraat car parks. They cost €1.50 per hour, up to a maximum of €5 a day (2026 rate). Parking is free on Sundays. Parking at Hotel Asteria is always free.
f3-v: Are the shops in Venray open on Sundays?
f3-a: Not every Sunday. On shopping Sundays the shops are open from 12 noon to 5 pm. This winter they are Sunday 29 November, 20 December and 27 December 2026. Each shop decides for itself whether to take part.
f4-v: What is there to see in the centre of Venray?
f4-a: The Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk on the Grote Markt, a late Gothic church with a large collection of statues. The Venrays Museum opposite is open from Wednesday to Sunday, 1.30 pm to 5 pm. The sculpture forest of the Odapark is a twenty-minute walk away and free.
f5-v: When is the weekly market in Venray?
f5-a: Every Monday from 11 am to 4 pm, on the Henseniusplein and the Schouwburgplein.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area after a day in town?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open from 4 pm to 10 pm Monday to Thursday and from 12 noon to 10 pm Friday to Sunday. Tuesday is swimwear day. You can have dinner in the brasserie until 9.30 pm.
